Rozado political preferences of LLMs PLOS ONE 2024 left-of-center

sources_considered.why: ACL 2024 paper testing how stable LLM opinions are.
Notes that base models answer incoherently and points to post-training as a source of stated preferences, which bears on the cause.

receipt.public_excerpt: We show that models give substantively different answers when not forced; that answers change depending on how models are forced; and that answers lack paraphrase robustness.

evidence_items.explanation: Supports the incoherence part for the models tested. It does not test whether conflicting training data is the cause.

receipt.public_excerpt: Though not conclusive, our results provide preliminary evidence for the intriguing hypothesis that the embedding of political preferences into LLMs might be happening mostly post-pretraining.

evidence_items.explanation: Suggests that stated views are shaped largely by fine-tuning, not only by pretraining data. That complicates the causal story, but it is preliminary and not about coherence directly.

unresolved_gaps: No study found tests whether LLM inconsistency comes from conflicting training data rather than other causes.
No evaluation covers every LLM, so 'no LLM is fully coherent' cannot be confirmed for all of them.
